A receipt proves what a named server sent, and when. Read it as exactly that. It does not prove * That the server told the truth. A receipt shows what api.weather.gov said, not the weather. * Anything about a server the operator controls. That receipt is still the operator’s word, now fixed in time and bytes. * That the agent sent every action through the witness. That takes credential custody or egress control. * Independence, when one party runs both the agent side and the witness. High-value receipts should carry more than one witness. * That the content is safe to act on. A genuine page can still carry a prompt injection. Engine limits today: TLS 1.2 only (TLS 1.3 is on TLSNotary’s roadmap), pre-release software, and no compressed or streamed responses. ## Two tools your agent already knows how to call. Histor ships as a CLI and an MCP server, so it works in Claude Code, Cursor and any MCP client. Receipts are content-addressed: agents pass a short receipt_id instead of 15 KB of base64. witnessed_fetch(url, fields?, mode?) GETs an https:// URL through a Histor witness. Returns the server, time, request and disclosed fields, plus a receipt_id. verify_receipt(receipt_id | receipt, expect_server?) Checks a receipt another agent handed you, offline. Returns what it proves, or the reason it fails. witnessed_request(url, method, body, request_fields?) POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE. Credentials for the target live on the server, so the model never sees a secret. The request body is committed and stays hidden unless you disclose named fields. New AI-liability covers ask for agent logs, and today those logs are self-reported. Cyber insurers learned to price from external scans the insured couldn’t edit. A Histor receipt gives an AI-liability book the same kind of signal for agent actions. ### At claim time Check what the agent was told before it acted. The claims desk verifies the receipt itself, offline. ### At underwriting Witnessed actions as a share of all agent actions is a number the insured can’t inflate. ### Narrow by design A receipt proves what a named server sent and when. It makes no claim about whether the agent acted well.
